html:
Leo VI, called the Wise, was Byzantine emperor from 886 to 912, the second ruler of the Macedonian dynasty. He was a scholar more than a soldier, known for his laws and writings.

He was the son of Basil I, though some at the time whispered that his real father was the murdered emperor Michael III. Basil disliked him and even had him jailed. On taking the throne he removed the patriarch Photios and put his own young brother in his place.

His works:

  • the Basilika, a revision of Justinian's law in sixty books of Greek, finishing work his father had begun;
  • more than a hundred new laws of his own;
  • the Book of the Eparch, rules for the guilds of Constantinople;
  • a handbook of war, sermons and poems.

His reign was less happy abroad. Simeon of Bulgaria beat his armies in the 890s, the Arabs took the last Byzantine stronghold in Sicily in 902 and sacked Thessalonica in 904, and after a Rus' attack he made a trade treaty with them in 911. At home, his fourth marriage, to the mother of his only son, the future Constantine VII, broke church law and caused a long quarrel with the church.
sum: Leo VI, called the Wise, was Byzantine emperor from 886 to 912, the second ruler of the Macedonian dynasty. He was a scholar more than a soldier, known for his laws and writings.
